continents.name: Africa
continents.description: The cradle of humanity — home to the Sahara, the Nile, and the savanna.

continents.name: Antarctica
continents.description: The frozen southernmost continent — no countries, just research stations.

continents.name: Asia
continents.description: The largest and most populous continent — home to the world's highest peak, Mount Everest.

continents.name: Europe
continents.description: A continent of many small countries packed with old cities, castles, and rivers.

continents.name: North America
continents.description: From the Arctic to the Caribbean — home of the Grand Canyon and the Great Lakes.

continents.name: Oceania
continents.description: Australia plus thousands of Pacific islands.

continents.name: South America
continents.description: Home to the Amazon rainforest and the Andes mountains.

countries.name: United Arab Emirates
countries.fact_card: Seven desert emirates united into one country — home of the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building.

countries.name: Afghanistan
countries.fact_card: A landlocked country at the crossroads of Central, South, and West Asia, home to the towering Hindu Kush mountains.

countries.name: Angola
countries.fact_card: A large country on Africa's southwestern Atlantic coast, rich in oil and diamonds, with dramatic waterfalls and a plateau interior.

countries.name: Argentina
countries.fact_card: Stretches from subtropical jungle in the north to the icy edge of Antarctica in the south.

countries.name: Austria
countries.fact_card: A landlocked country in the heart of Europe, famous for its Alpine ski slopes, classical music composers like Mozart and Beethoven, and the grand city of Vienna.

countries.name: Australia
countries.fact_card: Both a country and a continent — home to kangaroos, koalas, and the Great Barrier Reef.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
countries.fact_card: Sitting at the crossroads of Europe and Asia on the Caspian Sea, Azerbaijan is famous for its ancient fire temples — where flames once burned naturally from underground gas.

countries.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
countries.fact_card: A mountainous Balkan country famous for the Stari Most — a graceful 16th-century Ottoman stone bridge in Mostar — where divers leap into the river below.

countries.name: Bangladesh
countries.fact_card: One of the most densely populated countries on Earth, sitting on the world's largest river delta.

countries.name: Belgium
countries.fact_card: Headquarters of the European Union — famous for chocolate, waffles, beer, and comic-book heroes like Tintin.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
countries.fact_card: A flat, landlocked Sahel country in West Africa whose name means 'Land of the Honest People' — it sits at the edge of the expanding Sahara Desert.

countries.name: Bulgaria
countries.fact_card: A Balkan country on the Black Sea coast, home to the stunning Rila Monastery high in the mountains and one of the oldest rose-oil industries in the world.

countries.name: Brunei
countries.official_name: Nation of Brunei, Abode of Peace

countries.name: Bolivia
countries.fact_card: Home of the world's largest salt flat, which becomes a giant mirror in the rainy season.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.fact_card: Holds most of the Amazon rainforest and is the only country in South America that speaks Portuguese.

countries.name: Botswana
countries.fact_card: Home to the Okavango Delta, a vast inland wetland where the river evaporates into the Kalahari Desert instead of reaching the sea.

countries.name: Belarus
countries.fact_card: A flat, forested country in Eastern Europe known for its potato pancakes (draniki), medieval castles, and being one of Europe's last remaining untouched ancient forests at Białowieża.

countries.name: Canada
countries.fact_card: The world's second-largest country by area, with more lakes than the rest of the world combined.

countries.name: DR Congo
countries.fact_card: Home to the world's second-largest rainforest and the mighty Congo River — the deepest river on Earth — making it one of the most biodiverse places on the planet.

countries.name: Central African Republic
countries.fact_card: A remote landlocked country at the geographic heart of Africa, home to western lowland gorillas and forest elephants in some of the continent's most intact rainforests.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.fact_card: A landlocked alpine nation famous for neutrality, chocolate, and four official languages.

countries.name: Ivory Coast
countries.landmark: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace
countries.fact_card: The world's largest producer of cocoa beans, home of the planet's biggest church by area.

countries.name: Chile
countries.fact_card: A long, thin ribbon of a country stretching 2,700 miles down South America's Pacific coast.

countries.name: Cameroon
countries.fact_card: Nicknamed 'Africa in miniature' for packing deserts, rainforests, beaches, and mountains into one country.

countries.name: China
countries.fact_card: Home to the world's longest wall and, for centuries, the world's largest population.

countries.name: Colombia
countries.fact_card: The only South American country with coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea, and home to the lush Amazon rainforest in its south.

countries.name: Costa Rica
countries.fact_card: A small Central American country with no army; its motto is 'pura vida' and 25% of its land is protected wilderness.

countries.name: Cuba
countries.fact_card: The largest island in the Caribbean, famous for its music, vintage cars, and tropical beaches.

countries.name: Cape Verde
countries.fact_card: An archipelago of ten volcanic islands in the Atlantic off West Africa, famous for soulful morna music and its towering active volcano, Pico do Fogo.

countries.name: Curaçao
countries.fact_card: A Dutch Caribbean island known for the brightly painted colonial waterfront of Willemstad — a World Heritage site — and the vivid blue Curaçao liqueur made there.

countries.name: Czechia
countries.fact_card: A central European country famous for fairy-tale castles and the world's highest beer consumption per person.

countries.name: Germany
countries.fact_card: Once split in two by a wall through Berlin; reunified in 1990.

countries.name: Denmark
countries.fact_card: A tiny Scandinavian kingdom of 400 islands — the birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen and LEGO.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
countries.fact_card: Shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti — where Columbus founded the first European city in the Americas.

countries.name: Algeria
countries.fact_card: Africa's largest country by area, with 80% of its land covered by the Sahara Desert.

countries.name: Ecuador
countries.fact_card: Named for the equator that runs through it; gateway to the unique animals of the Galápagos Islands.

countries.name: Egypt
countries.fact_card: Built one of the world's oldest civilizations along the Nile, the longest river on Earth.

countries.name: Spain
countries.fact_card: Sits on the Iberian Peninsula and once ruled an empire that spanned the Americas.

countries.name: Ethiopia
countries.fact_card: Birthplace of coffee, one of the oldest Christian nations, and home of 'Lucy,' a 3.2-million-year-old human ancestor.

countries.name: Finland
countries.fact_card: Land of a thousand lakes and the northern lights — voted the world's happiest country many years in a row.

countries.name: Fiji
countries.fact_card: An archipelago of 333 South Pacific islands surrounded by coral reefs and warm turquoise waters.

countries.name: France
countries.fact_card: The world's most-visited country, with mountains, coastlines, and overseas territories on five continents.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.official_name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
countries.fact_card: An island nation made of four countries: England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

countries.name: Georgia
countries.fact_card: A small country tucked in the Caucasus Mountains between Europe and Asia, with a unique ancient alphabet, cave cities, and one of the world's oldest wine-making traditions.

countries.name: Ghana
countries.fact_card: The first sub-Saharan African country to win independence; producer of some of the world's best cocoa.

countries.name: Guinea
countries.fact_card: Often called 'the water tower of West Africa' — nearly all of West Africa's major rivers, including the Niger, originate in Guinea's central highlands.

countries.name: Greece
countries.fact_card: Birthplace of the Olympic Games and home to over 6,000 islands scattered across two seas.

countries.name: Guatemala
countries.fact_card: Heart of the ancient Maya civilization, with active volcanoes and the deep-blue Lake Atitlán.

countries.name: Honduras
countries.fact_card: A Central American country with ancient Maya ruins, lush cloud forests, and the world's second-largest barrier reef.

countries.name: Croatia
countries.fact_card: Famous for its Adriatic coast of more than 1,000 islands and the medieval walled city of Dubrovnik.

countries.name: Haiti
countries.fact_card: The world's first nation founded by a successful slave revolution, sharing the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.

countries.name: Hungary
countries.fact_card: A landlocked country in central Europe whose language isn't related to any of its neighbors.

countries.name: Indonesia
countries.fact_card: An archipelago of more than 17,000 islands — the world's largest island nation.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.fact_card: The 'Emerald Isle,' famous for endless green pastures, traditional music, and St. Patrick's Day.

countries.name: Israel
countries.fact_card: A tiny nation at the crossroads of three continents, sacred to Jews, Christians, and Muslims.

countries.name: India
countries.fact_card: The world's most populous democracy and home to 22 official languages.

countries.name: Iraq
countries.fact_card: Birthplace of civilization in Mesopotamia, the 'land between two rivers' — the Tigris and the Euphrates.

countries.name: Iran
countries.fact_card: Heir to the ancient Persian Empire, with deserts, snow-capped mountains, and the world's best saffron.

countries.name: Iceland
countries.fact_card: A volcanic island just below the Arctic Circle, with glaciers, geysers, and active volcanoes.

countries.name: Italy
countries.fact_card: Shaped like a boot kicking the island of Sicily; home of the Roman Empire.

countries.name: Jamaica
countries.fact_card: Birthplace of reggae music and Bob Marley, with some of the Caribbean's most stunning beaches.

countries.name: Jordan
countries.fact_card: Home of Petra, the rose-red city carved into cliffs by the ancient Nabataeans.

countries.name: Japan
countries.fact_card: A chain of more than 14,000 islands; the sun on its flag represents Japan as 'land of the rising sun.'

countries.name: Kenya
countries.fact_card: Crossed by the equator, home to the world's most famous safari grounds and the cradle of human evolution.

countries.name: Cambodia
countries.fact_card: Home to Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument on Earth, built by the Khmer Empire 900 years ago.

countries.name: Kiribati
countries.official_name: Independent and Sovereign Republic of Kiribati

countries.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
countries.official_name: Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis

countries.name: North Korea
countries.fact_card: The northern half of the Korean Peninsula, separated from South Korea since 1953, with rugged mountains and Mount Paektu — a sacred volcano — on its northern border.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.fact_card: Famous worldwide for K-pop and K-dramas; shares a tense border with North Korea.

countries.name: Kuwait
countries.fact_card: A small but wealthy country at the top of the Persian Gulf, sitting atop some of the world's largest oil reserves, with iconic water towers that store desalinated water.

countries.name: Kazakhstan
countries.fact_card: The world's largest landlocked country — bigger than Western Europe — with vast empty steppes, deserts, and the historic Baikonur launch site where the first human went to space.

countries.name: Laos
countries.fact_card: The only landlocked country in Southeast Asia, Laos is crisscrossed by the Mekong River and dotted with ancient Buddhist temples draped in saffron-orange.

countries.name: Lebanon
countries.fact_card: A small mountainous country on the Mediterranean, named for its towering cedar trees that grace its national flag.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
countries.official_name: Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka
countries.fact_card: A teardrop-shaped island south of India, famous for cinnamon, tea, and ancient Buddhist temples.

countries.name: Liberia
countries.fact_card: Founded in 1847 by formerly enslaved Americans returning to Africa, Liberia was the first African republic — its flag echoes the Stars and Stripes of the United States.

countries.name: Lithuania
countries.fact_card: A small Baltic nation — the first Soviet republic to declare independence — covered in pine forests and pristine lakes.

countries.name: Libya
countries.fact_card: Nearly all desert, but holds some of the world's best-preserved ancient Roman ruins along its Mediterranean coast.

countries.name: Morocco
countries.fact_card: Where the Atlas Mountains meet the Sahara and the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean.

countries.name: Madagascar
countries.fact_card: The world's fourth-largest island, where most plants and animals — including lemurs — exist nowhere else.

countries.name: Mali
countries.fact_card: Ancient home of the Mali Empire and the legendary city of Timbuktu — a center of trans-Saharan trade and Islamic scholarship.

countries.name: Myanmar
countries.official_name: Republic of the Union of Myanmar
countries.fact_card: Land of thousands of golden pagodas, with the Irrawaddy River flowing through its heart.

countries.name: Mongolia
countries.fact_card: The world's most sparsely populated country, with nomadic herders riding the same vast steppes as Genghis Khan's empire.

countries.name: Mauritania
countries.fact_card: Covering mostly Sahara Desert, Mauritania is home to ancient fortified cities (ksour) that were once crucial stops on trans-Saharan camel caravan trading routes.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.fact_card: Home of the ancient Maya and Aztec civilizations and the birthplace of chocolate.

countries.name: Malaysia
countries.fact_card: Split into two parts by the South China Sea, with rainforests, twin skyscrapers, and orangutans.

countries.name: Mozambique
countries.fact_card: A long, narrow country stretching down southeast Africa's coast, with over 2,500 km of Indian Ocean shoreline and some of Africa's best coral reefs.

countries.name: Niger
countries.fact_card: One of the world's largest countries by area, Niger is mostly Sahara Desert in the north and dry Sahel savanna in the south, centered around the Niger River.

countries.name: Nigeria
countries.fact_card: Africa's most populous country, with over 500 languages spoken.

countries.name: Nicaragua
countries.fact_card: Central America's largest country, with a chain of active volcanoes running along its Pacific coast and the largest lake in Central America, Lake Nicaragua.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.fact_card: About a third of the country lies below sea level, protected by an enormous system of dikes.

countries.name: Norway
countries.fact_card: Carved by glaciers, Norway's coast is a maze of fjords and one of the world's longest coastlines.

countries.name: Nepal
countries.fact_card: Home to Mount Everest, the world's tallest peak, and eight of the world's ten highest mountains. The only country with a non-rectangular flag.

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.fact_card: Two main islands shaped by volcanoes and glaciers — home of the kiwi bird and the Māori people.

countries.name: Oman
countries.fact_card: An ancient seafaring nation on the southeastern tip of the Arabian Peninsula, with dramatic fjords in the north, vast sand dunes, and a history of frankincense trade.

countries.name: Panama
countries.fact_card: Home of the Panama Canal — a 51-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.

countries.name: Peru
countries.fact_card: Home of Machu Picchu and the Inca Empire, spanning desert coast, Andes peaks, and Amazon rainforest.

countries.name: Papua New Guinea
countries.official_name: Independent State of Papua New Guinea
countries.fact_card: One of the most culturally diverse countries on Earth, where over 800 languages are spoken.

countries.name: Philippines
countries.fact_card: An archipelago of 7,641 islands with one of the most diverse marine ecosystems on Earth.

countries.name: Pakistan
countries.fact_card: Home to K2, the second-highest mountain on Earth, and one of the world's most populous countries.

countries.name: Poland
countries.fact_card: Home to Europe's last primeval forest and the birthplace of scientist Marie Curie.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.fact_card: From this small country, explorers like Vasco da Gama opened up sea routes around the world.

countries.name: Paraguay
countries.landmark: Jesuit Missions of La Santísima Trinidad
countries.fact_card: A landlocked South American country where both Spanish and Guaraní (an indigenous language) are spoken by nearly everyone.

countries.name: Qatar
countries.fact_card: A tiny desert peninsula that hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup, sitting on one of the world's largest natural gas reserves.

countries.name: Romania
countries.fact_card: Home of the Carpathian Mountains and the legend of Dracula, inspired by 15th-century prince Vlad the Impaler.

countries.name: Serbia
countries.fact_card: A landlocked Balkan country at the confluence of the Sava and Danube rivers, with a 7,000-year history of civilization.

countries.name: Russia
countries.fact_card: The largest country on Earth, stretching across 11 time zones.

countries.name: Rwanda
countries.fact_card: Nicknamed 'Land of a Thousand Hills,' home to endangered mountain gorillas in misty volcanic forests.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
countries.fact_card: Holds Islam's two holiest cities, Mecca and Medina, and vast deserts of sand and oil.

countries.name: Solomon Islands
countries.fact_card: An archipelago of nearly 1,000 islands in the South Pacific, with WWII history and pristine coral reefs.

countries.name: Sudan
countries.fact_card: Holds more pyramids than Egypt — built by the ancient Kingdom of Kush along the Nile.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.fact_card: One of the most forested countries in Europe, with a coastline scattered with 30,000 islands.

countries.name: Singapore
countries.fact_card: A tiny island city-state with one of the world's busiest ports — went from fishing village to global hub in 60 years.

countries.name: Slovakia
countries.fact_card: A landlocked Central European country with hundreds of medieval castles — more castles per square kilometer than almost anywhere in the world.

countries.name: Senegal
countries.fact_card: Westernmost country in mainland Africa, famous for music, wrestling, and the welcoming spirit of 'teranga.'

countries.name: Somalia
countries.fact_card: Located on the Horn of Africa, Somalia has the longest coastline of any African country, and its ancient cave paintings at Laas Geel are among the oldest in the world.

countries.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
countries.official_name: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe

countries.name: El Salvador
countries.fact_card: The smallest and most densely populated country in Central America, nicknamed 'The Land of Volcanoes' — its stuffed corn cakes (pupusas) are the national dish.

countries.name: Chad
countries.fact_card: A vast landlocked country where the Sahara Desert in the north gives way to a green Sahel belt in the south, and where ancient cave art dots the otherworldly Ennedi Plateau.

countries.name: Thailand
countries.fact_card: Known as the 'Land of Smiles' — the only Southeast Asian country never colonized by Europeans.

countries.name: Tajikistan
countries.fact_card: Over 90% of this Central Asian country is covered by mountains — including the soaring Pamirs, nicknamed 'the Roof of the World,' with peaks over 7,000 metres.

countries.name: Tunisia
countries.fact_card: Africa's northernmost country, where ancient Carthage once challenged the Roman Empire.

countries.name: Turkey
countries.fact_card: Bridges Europe and Asia — Istanbul is the only major city sitting on two continents.

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.fact_card: A mountainous island off the coast of China, known for night markets, tech giants, and oolong tea.

countries.name: Tanzania
countries.fact_card: Home of Mount Kilimanjaro — Africa's highest peak — and the Serengeti's great wildebeest migration.

countries.name: Ukraine
countries.fact_card: Europe's largest country fully on the continent, covered by some of the world's richest farmland.

countries.name: Uganda
countries.fact_card: Source of the Nile and a refuge for mountain gorillas in the misty Bwindi Forest.

countries.name: United States
countries.fact_card: Spans four time zones in the mainland and includes the world's first national park, Yellowstone.

countries.name: Uruguay
countries.fact_card: A small South American country with vast cattle ranches and the most World Cup soccer trophies per person.

countries.name: Uzbekistan
countries.fact_card: Home to the ancient Silk Road cities of Samarkand and Bukhara — once the most dazzling trading stops in the medieval world — now gleaming with turquoise-tiled mosques.

countries.name: Venezuela
countries.fact_card: Home of Angel Falls — the world's tallest waterfall, plunging from a flat-topped mountain in the Amazon.

countries.name: Vietnam
countries.fact_card: An S-shaped country along the South China Sea, famous for rice terraces and pho noodle soup.

countries.name: Samoa
countries.fact_card: A pair of large volcanic islands in the South Pacific, home to one of the world's oldest Polynesian cultures.

countries.name: Yemen
countries.fact_card: On the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula, Yemen is home to Socotra — an island so isolated it evolved alien-looking 'dragon blood' trees found nowhere else on Earth.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.fact_card: Has three capital cities and is home to the world's deepest gold mines.

countries.name: Zambia
countries.fact_card: A landlocked country in southern Africa that shares Victoria Falls — one of the world's greatest waterfalls — with its neighbor Zimbabwe.

countries.name: Zimbabwe
countries.fact_card: Home to Victoria Falls — one of the world's largest waterfalls — and the medieval stone ruins of Great Zimbabwe.

world_cup_2026.label: World Cup 2026
world_cup_2026.note: The 47 nations of the 2026 FIFA World Cup that exist as distinct entries in our atlas. Scotland is omitted (part of the UK; England maps to GB). Curaçao (CW) is included as a backfilled non-sovereign entry.
